tasks.short: Monitor menu spending and meal economy

steps.what: Gather current menus spending records and meal volumes
Monitor menus and spending against available budget and actual kitchen conditions
Choose practical changes to keep meal preparation economical

tasks.design: Configure a menu/spending view in {OTHER} kitchen management software from existing records. The cook checks current figures and still observes actual preparation and decides what changes are sensible; low cost alone does not establish a suitable meal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Menu and spending references need repeated collation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native kitchen reports can show existing cost and meal data together.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing economy with diet, food quality and actual serving demand.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a numerical variance reflects waste, demand or a necessary meal choice.
tasks.altitude: Less reference gathering; menu and preparation judgement stay unchanged.

reach.task: Evaluate proposed menu changes within budget and service requirements
reach.learn: Which costs the cook can influence without reducing meal suitability

evidence.claim: Apicbase links recipes with supplier prices and updates recipe costs as prices change; this supports native kitchen costing reports, not the estimated monitoring saving.
The proposed monitoring view and time split are unmeasured assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring existing menu/spending information, excluding its original record capture and physical meal preparation.

Existing kitchen records produced by the cook's recordkeeping process provide period, menu/recipe version, food expenditure and meal counts; existing finance processing provides invoice amounts. Their capture time remains unchanged and must be allocated once in a roll-up.
s1 counts reference selection, current-period checks and manual collation for missing data; no new free cost-per-meal or waste code is assumed.
s2 retains observation and interpretation; s3 retains all proposed-change judgement.
Test native reports first. Incomplete or mismatched periods use manual records without silently imputing figures.
unknowns: Available records and actual time spent gathering them
research_questions: Can existing reports reduce reference gathering after period and completeness checks?

already_counted.description: Reference checking and manual fallback in s1

incremental.description: Maintain report filters and inspect missing-period problems

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=12.5+45+30=87.5; gross 12.5 minus 1 upkeep gives net 11.5. High needs compatible existing records; low covers missing records and manual collation. Upstream capture earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather food use observations stock counts and expenditure documents
outputs: dated food use entries and spending sources

steps.what: Compile and maintain records of food use and expenditures
inputs: dated food use entries and spending sources
outputs: compiled food use and expenditure record

steps.what: Reconcile compiled records with counts and spending sources and correct discrepancies
inputs: compiled food use and expenditure record
dated food use entries and spending sources
outputs: checked food use and expenditure record

tasks.design: Configure food-use records in {OTHER} kitchen management software with reusable items, units and supported invoice imports. The cook still captures physical usage and checks the completed record; automatic compilation does not replace stock counts or reconciliation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source observations and receipts are rewritten into a separate summary.
tasks.enabler_now: Native records forms and supported imports can reuse captured values and assemble the ledger.
tasks.still_hard: Missing usage, unit mismatches and spending that belongs to another period.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining discrepancies using actual kitchen events.
tasks.altitude: Less record compilation; source capture and reconciliation stay with the cook.

reach.task: Resolve an expenditure document that does not match the kitchen record
reach.learn: How receipt, invoice and accounting periods differ

evidence.claim: Native records forms and explicit unit mappings can reduce recopying; the proposed food-use compilation saving is model knowledge and not a digest case result.

assumptions: Boundary is the cook's food use/expenditure record, excluding finance posting, procurement and physical preparation.
s1 counts all observation and capture of date, item, issue/return quantity, unit, stock count and receipt/invoice reference with amount; the cook is the producer.
Existing suppliers produce invoices during unchanged sales fulfilment; the finance process produces any existing electronic invoice export. No additional supplier capture is required.
s2 retains selecting/matching items, entering unsupported sources and resolving unit mappings; no waste sensor, structured discrepancy code or complete usage feed is assumed.
Test native forms/imports first. Missing or unclear sources stay manual and are reconciled in retained s3 time.
Recordkeeping feeds may support monitoring, but overlapping actions must be assigned once rather than summing both task baselines.
unknowns: Current recopying burden, native imports and unit consistency
research_questions: How much compilation time remains after retaining all physical capture and discrepancy checks?

already_counted.description: Record entry/matching and unsupported-source handling in s2
Full reconciliation and corrections in s3

incremental.description: Maintain local item/unit mappings and inspect import failures

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=43+11.1+20=74.1; gross 25.9 minus 2 focal upkeep gives net 23.9. High needs repeat items and usable sources; low covers manual receipts and unit exceptions consuming the benefit. Finance upkeep stays separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confirm recipe quantities yields and current ingredient prices
Calculate ingredient costs and candidate meal prices
outputs: calculated meal cost and candidate price

steps.what: Review calculations and determine the meal price within pricing policy
inputs: calculated meal cost and candidate price
outputs: determined meal price or price recommendation

tasks.design: Configure recipe costing in {OTHER} kitchen management software so checked ingredient prices flow into explicit quantity/yield calculations. The cook checks mappings and still determines the appropriate price under existing policy; no model selects an unsupported margin.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ingredient prices and recipe values require repeated copying between calculation sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recipe costing can reuse ingredient-price links and recalculate deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Actual yield, substitutions and institutional pricing constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether the calculated cost represents how the meal is really prepared.
tasks.altitude: Less price recopying and calculation maintenance; pricing authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Check whether the proposed price fits the service's budget and policy
reach.learn: How subsidies or service constraints affect meal prices

evidence.claim: Apicbase links recipes to supplier prices and updates costs when ingredient prices change.
The labour estimate is an unmeasured scenario and is not supported by a costing time-saving case in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is calculating and determining a meal price, excluding publishing prices, purchasing and original recipe development.

s1 counts confirmation/capture of ingredient identity, quantity/unit, batch yield, supplier pack quantity/unit, effective price/date and permitted pricing rule; the cook is the producer of checked costing inputs.
Supplier price sources originate in existing supplier sales records; no new structured feed is assumed. s1/s2 retain manual entry and mapping when supported import is unavailable.
s2 reduces repeated copying and sheet setup, not existing formula runtime; missing yield or incompatible units require manual correction rather than inference.
Test native recipe costing before custom code. s3 retains full reasonableness and policy review; no final published price is changed automatically.
unknowns: Recipe structure, current automatic calculations and native price imports
research_questions: Does native costing reduce actual human recopying after counting recipe and pack-unit checks?

already_counted.description: Mapping and manual source exceptions in s2
Cost and price review in s3

incremental.description: Maintain recipe-price links and inspect unit/yield changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+10+25=70; gross 30 minus 1.5 upkeep gives net 28.5. High needs repeated manual price updates; low covers already-linked calculations or substantial yield/pack corrections consuming the benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce record collation and costing repetition while retaining economic and food judgement.
reach: Discuss checked costs and discrepancies with finance and kitchen supervisors
role.ambitious_version: Use dependable records to propose economical meals without weakening suitability or safety.
